context: Request: all the firm's merger agreements that use the phrase 'material adverse effect', pulling those documents (for an MAE language bank). Rubric: nine matters (1001-00004, 1001-00005, 1003-00003, 1003-00004, 1008-00008, 1018-00003, 1032-00005, 1041-00003, 1042-00004), each with its executed merger agreement file named, plus precision.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Whole-store glob; the agent names candidates from the capped listing. The review asks for a full listing and a text scan.

stages.stage: Search file names for a document type
stages.note: declared: List files in the document store (attempt 2). Script listing, per matter, only files under transaction-document folders (about 99K characters, cut in the log). The review flags the folder filter and the truncation.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Store-wide extraction for the phrase times out with a per-file parsing bug, printing about 243K characters of error lines. The review reports goal not reached.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Attempt 2: corrected store-wide threaded scan times out with no output.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Attempt 3: after an indentation error, a scan of the first matter-number batch lists hit files.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Attempt 4: next batch written to a file; shows only the first lines. The review flags the 342 hit paths never viewed.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Attempt 5: next batch; the review flags filtering hits by agreement-like names.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Attempt 6: next batch; two merger-agreement files shown.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Attempt 7: last batch; the agent keeps agreement-named paths as candidates.

stages.note: Reads the opening of 13 candidate merger and business-combination agreements, one per matter.

stages.stage: Search within a candidate matter's files
stages.note: Snippet script over the 13 candidate matters printing every phrase hit with surrounding text and no cap; about 5.6M characters fill the context before the stage is closed, and no deliverable is written.

runs.failure_point: After finding all candidate merger agreements, an uncapped snippet script over the candidate matters printed about 5.6M characters and filled the context before any answer was written.

first_error.stage: Search within a candidate matter's files
first_error.critic_note: The run ended inside the stage, before stage_end; earlier reviews had asked to cap output per file.
first_error.why: The snippet script printed every phrase occurrence with context from all documents of 13 matters with no output cap, so the result filled the context and the run ended with no response written.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Whole-store glob in parallel with a two-level folder listing (80 lines) and file-type counts.

stages.stage: Search file names for request keywords
stages.note: find | grep for merger and acquisition agreement names (162 paths), a content grep on *.docx for the phrase that returns nothing, and a folder count; the protocol's stage check notes the grep does not fit the open stage.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Store-wide and range scans time out three times; then a scan over files with merger-agreement names and a file-name search for other agreement names. The review flags the file-name restriction.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Attempt 2: background store-wide scan polled to completion (1,278 hits in 169 matters), then filters hits by agreement names.

stages.note: declared: Scan document text with an extraction script (attempt 3). Checks scan errors and searches hit paths and store paths for other agreement-like names.

divergence: All three runs reached every needed matter through a store-wide phrase scan and opened the candidate agreements. They split after screening: T1 and T2 tallied the hits per file from their saved scan output and wrote the list (pass), while T0, which had scanned in seven separate batches, ran a final snippet script over all documents of its 13 candidate matters with no output cap; the result filled the context before stage_end, so no review ran and no answer was written. Earlier reviews in T0 had asked to cap output per file.
